title: Evidence matrix: 27 studies × 6 finding dimensions — GPT-6.1-Sol · Extra High
question: What empirical studies have compared LLM-generated scientific peer review with human peer review, and what did each study find about agreement, error detection, recall, score bias, overconfidence, and limitations?

citation.title: GPT4 is Slightly Helpful for Peer-Review Assistance: A Pilot Study

rows.design_and_sample: 10 volunteer authors; 1 declined AI review; nine human reviews discussed. Separate perturbation test: 20 NeurIPS submissions, 10 accepted/10 rejected.
rows.evaluated_models: GPT-4: 8k user study; 4k and 32k perturbation conditions

agreement.finding: Helpfulness comparison is not reviewer agreement; GPT 3.0±0.96 versus humans 3.1±0.57 (95% CIs, 1–5 scale).

error_detection.finding: Synthetic abstract contradiction detected in 70% (4k) versus 35% (32k); informal sentence in 60% versus 5%; 20 papers per condition.

recall.finding: Synthetic perturbation recall: abstract 0.70±0.21/0.35±0.21; sentence 0.60±0.22/0.05±0.10 (4k/32k, 95% CIs). Not human-comment or real-error recall.

score_bias.finding: Not measured.

overconfidence.finding: No confidence calibration or adjudicated false-positive rate.

limitations.finding: Small volunteer sample; generic critiques, missed instructions and detail. Author helpfulness does not establish gatekeeping competence.

citation.title: Can large language models provide useful feedback on research papers? A large-scale empirical analysis

rows.publication_status: published in NEJM AI 1(8), 2024; full text extracted from author preprint

source_version.note: Only arXiv version; publisher full-text endpoint failed. DOI 10.1056/AIoa2400196.

rows.design_and_sample: 3,096 accepted Nature-family papers; 1,709 ICLR papers; 308 researcher respondents from 110 US institutions.
rows.evaluated_models: GPT-4

agreement.finding: Per-reviewer overlap (denominator GPT comments): Nature 30.85% versus human–human 28.58%; ICLR 39.23% versus 35.25%; comment count controlled.

error_detection.finding: Comment overlap and author usefulness were measured; no independently verified scientific-error detection benchmark.

recall.finding: Human-comment recovery increased with reviewer consensus: Nature 11.39%,20.67%,31.67% for comments raised by 1,2,≥3 humans. This is comment coverage, not error recall.

score_bias.finding: Not measured.

overconfidence.finding: Unmatched AI comments were not adjudicated as false positives; no direct confidence calibration.

limitations.finding: 57.4% found feedback helpful/very helpful; 82.4% at least as useful as some humans. Generic, shallow technical critiques; self-selection, one model, text/caption input.

citations.location: Fig.4; Discussion; Limitations of LLM feedback, pp.5–8

citation.title: ReviewerGPT? An Exploratory Study on Using Large Language Models for Paper Reviewing

rows.design_and_sample: 13 deliberately flawed short CS papers; 119 checklist–paper pairs from 15 NeurIPS papers; 10 controlled abstract pairs.
rows.evaluated_models: GPT-4 main; Bard, Vicuna, Koala, Alpaca, LLaMa, Dolly, OpenAssistant, StableLM pilot

agreement.finding: Checklist accuracy 86.6% on 119 pairs, majority of 3 responses against authors’ manual ground truth; authors’ answers also 86.6%. Not free-review agreement.

error_detection.finding: Detected planted errors in 7/13 short papers using any success across 3 prompts×3 responses; all 6 misses required knowledge beyond supplied proof.

recall.finding: Synthetic error success 7/13; disagreed with 75% of erroneous author checklist answers. Not broad recall of real peer-review errors.

score_bias.finding: Selected inferior abstract in 6/10 controlled pairs; failures included positive-result and bombastic-language preference, algorithm-name influence, prompt injection.

overconfidence.finding: Authors directly identify false positives: correct passages sometimes called incorrect; no aggregate false-positive rate or confidence calibration.

limitations.finding: Constructed short papers; narrow checklist task and text-only evidence. Figures made half the checklist errors indeterminable from input; no end-to-end human reviewer comparison.

rows.candidate_label: Are we there yet? (Ye et al.)

citation.title: Are We There Yet? Revealing the Risks of Utilizing Large Language Models in Scholarly Peer Review

rows.design_and_sample: ICLR corpus; 100-paper manipulation sample; 1,000-paper length tests; simulations of ranking effects.
rows.evaluated_models: GPT-4o main; Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, DeepSeek-V2.5 robustness; LLM Review, AI Scientist, AgentReview systems

agreement.finding: Human-matched fraction of AI points fell 53.29%→15.91% after prompt injection; coverage of human points fell 18.57%→5.09%.

error_detection.finding: No gold real-error detection task; manipulation and incomplete-input tests.

recall.finding: Human-comment coverage 18.57%→5.09% under injection; disclosed limitations echoed 4.5× more consistently by LLM than human reviews. Neither is error recall.

score_bias.finding: Injection raised LLM Review ratings 5.33→7.99 (10-point conversion); title+abstract+intro scored 5.11 vs full 5.34. Length/prestige preferences also observed.

overconfidence.finding: Unsupported-claim evidence: empty input elicited praise for novel methodology and writing in LLM Review; other systems recognized emptiness. No confidence calibration.

limitations.finding: Ratings often inferred from review text by Review2Rating; ranking simulation is hypothetical. Authors recommend supplemental use and manipulation safeguards.

citation.title: Evaluating science: A comparison of human and AI reviewers
citation.authors: Anna Shcherbiak; Hooman Habibnia; Robert Böhm; Susann Fiedler

rows.design_and_sample: 305 consenting human-written +20 fabricated abstracts; matched analysis 245 (225 human+20 AI); 217 participating human reviewers.
rows.evaluated_models: GPT-4 reviewer; GPT-3.5 abstract generator; GPTZero detector

agreement.finding: Quality correlation AI–human r=.23 (n=245) vs human–human r=.38 (n=231). Paper reports κ as 22% and 20.8% respectively; not raw exact agreement.

rows.evaluated_models: GPT-4-0613; MARG-S and single/multi-agent baselines

agreement.finding: Overlap precision MARG-S 4.41% vs human 12.00%, under strict semantic/specificity matching. These are reference overlap, not factual correctness.

error_detection.finding: No exhaustive adjudicated scientific-error detection task; author-rated critique accuracy was measured.

citation.title: When AI Co-Scientists Fail: SPOT—a Benchmark for Automated Verification of Scientific Research

rows.design_and_sample: 83 manuscripts with 91 author-acknowledged real errors, drawn from self-retractions and PubPeer; eight independent trials per model. Text-only ablation:48 figure-independent instances.
rows.evaluated_models: o3; GPT-4.1; Gemini2.5Pro/2.0FlashLite; Claude3.7Sonnet thinking/nonthinking; Qwen2.5VL72B/32B; Llama4Maverick/Scout; text-only DeepSeekR1/V3 and Qwen3-235B

rows.design_and_sample: 165 ICLR2026 papers (150 stratified+15 archive-recovered);9,900 reviews;145 detectability-verified injected errors across55 manuscripts; identity,input modality,integrity and prompting factorial conditions.

agreement.finding: Editor decisions match venue60.6%, exactly the naive mean-rating≥6 baseline; not criticism-content agreement.

error_detection.finding: Verified planted errors detected12.1% natural prompt versus22.2% verification-oriented prompt (145 errors, pooled conditions); providing figures reduces detection, text-only OR1.53,p=7.9e−7.

recall.finding: Synthetic-error recall natural→verification: Qwen text.11→.22,with figures.06→.16; Pixtral text.18→.25,figures.14→.25. Trend-reversal detection0 in both models/modalities.

score_bias.finding: Human means3.4/5.4/6.8 for reject/borderline/accept; blind text-only AI7.0–7.2. Figures addQwen .5–.9,Pixtral .1–.2; author prestige has no significant effect.

overconfidence.finding: Direct unsupported-observation finding: text-only reviews describe unprovided figures. Abstract claims “half”, but no audit denominator or detailed result table is supplied; no self-confidence calibration.

limitations.finding: Two models/one venue; synthetic errors; same-family LLM detection judge with human validation. Version-matched input provenance checked. Listed July31 date differs from August arXiv-ID prefix; retained as listed.

agreement.finding: Recommendations differed sharply; paper reports distributions and comment ratings rather than paired agreement coefficient.

error_detection.finding: Critical-analysis scores were evaluated, not verified-error detection.
